questions.q: What did Jesus send two of his disciples to do in the village opposite them?
questions.a: Jesus sent them to bring a colt to him that had never been ridden.

questions.q: What happened when the disciples untied the colt?
questions.a: Some people asked the disciples what they were doing, so they spoke to the people as Jesus told them, and the people let them go their way.

questions.q: What did the people spread on the road as Jesus rode on the colt?
questions.a: On the road the people spread their garments and branches they had cut from the fields.

questions.q: What coming kingdom were the people shouting about as Jesus rode toward Jerusalem?
questions.a: The people were shouting that the kingdom of their father David was coming.

questions.q: What did Jesus do when he entered the temple area?
questions.a: Jesus looked around and then went out to Bethany.

questions.q: What did Jesus do when he saw the fig tree with no fruit on it?
questions.a: Jesus said to the fig tree, “No one will ever eat fruit from you.”

questions.q: What did Jesus do when he entered the temple area this time?
questions.a: Jesus cast out the sellers and purchasers and would not allow anyone to carry merchandise through the temple.

questions.q: What did Jesus say the temple was supposed to be, according to Scripture?
questions.a: Jesus said that the temple was supposed to be a house of prayer for all the nations.

questions.q: What did Jesus say the chief priests and scribes had made the temple?
questions.a: Jesus said they had made the temple a den of robbers.

questions.q: What were the chief priests and scribes trying to do to Jesus?
questions.a: The chief priests and scribes were trying to kill Jesus.

questions.q: What happened to the fig tree to which Jesus had spoken?
questions.a: The fig tree to which Jesus had spoken withered away to its roots.

questions.q: What did Jesus say about everything we ask for in prayer?
questions.a: Jesus said that everything we ask for in prayer, believe that we have received it, and it will be ours.

questions.q: What did Jesus say we must do so that the Father in heaven will also forgive you?
questions.a: Jesus said we must forgive whatever we have against anyone so that the Father will also forgive us.

questions.q: In the temple, what did the chief priests, scribes, and elders want to know from Jesus?
questions.a: They wanted to know by what authority he did the things he was doing.

questions.q: What question did Jesus ask the chief priests, scribes, and elders?
questions.a: Jesus asked them if John’s baptism was from heaven or from men.

questions.q: Why did the chief priests, scribes, and elders not want to answer that John’s baptism was from heaven?
questions.a: They did not want to give this answer because Jesus would ask why they did not believe John.

questions.q: Why did the chief priests, scribes, and elders not want to answer that John’s baptism was from men?
questions.a: They did not want to give this answer because they feared the people, who all believed that John was a prophet.

commentary.text: The barren fig-tree cursed, The temple cleansed.
The priests and elders questioned concerning John the Baptist.

Verses 1–11 Christ's coming into Jerusalem thus remarkably, shows that he was not afraid of the power and malice of his enemies. This would encourage his disciples who were full of fear. Also, that he was not disquieted at the thoughts of his approaching sufferings. But all marked his humiliation; and these matters teach us not to mind high things, but to condescend to those of low estate. How ill it becomes Christians to take state, when Christ was so far from claiming it! They welcomed his person; Blessed is he that cometh, the “He that should come,” so often promised, so long expected; he comes in the name of the Lord. Let him have our best affections; he is a blessed Saviour, and brings blessings to us, and blessed be He that sent him. Praises be to our God, who is in the highest heavens, over all, God blessed for ever.

Christ looked to find some fruit, for the time of gathering figs, though it was near, was not yet come; but he found none. He made this fig-tree an example, not to the trees, but to the men of that generation. It was a figure of the doom upon the Jewish church, to which he came seeking fruit, but found none. Christ went to the temple, and began to reform the abuses in its courts, to show that when the Redeemer came to Zion, it was to turn away ungodliness from Jacob. The scribes and the chief priests sought, not how they might make their peace with him, but how they might destroy him. A desperate attempt, which they could not but fear was fighting against God.

The disciples could not think why that fig-tree should so soon wither away; but all wither who reject Christ; it represented the state of the Jewish church. We should rest in no religion that does not make us fruitful in good works. Christ taught them from hence to pray in faith. It may be applied to that mighty faith with which all true Christians are endued, and which does wonders in spiritual things. It justifies us, and so removes mountains of guilt, never to rise up in judgment against us. It purifies the heart, and so removes mountains of corruption, and makes them plain before the grace of God. One great errand to the throne of grace is to pray for the pardon of our sins; and care about this ought to be our daily concern.

Our Saviour shows how near akin his doctrine and baptism were to those of John; they had the same design and tendency, to bring in the gospel kingdom. These elders did not deserve to be taught; for it was plain that they contended not for truth, but victory: nor did he need to tell them; for the works he did, told them plainly he had authority from God; since no man could do the miracles which he did, unless God were with him.
